case.title: Bug 03 QA Report — ShopLite
case.summary: Bug in src/delivery/estimate.ts line 34: dispatch cutoff compared orderedAt.getUTCHours() (UTC) instead of ist.getUTCHours() (IST), causing orders placed after 20:00 IST but before midnight UTC to miss the cutoff and deliver one day early. Fix: change orderedAt to ist on that single line. Repro test (tests/bugproof/bug-03-delivery-estimate.test.ts) confirmed RED before fix and GREEN after. Full suite: 113/113 passed. Critic approved.

plainSummary.text: The delivery estimate feature calculated the wrong delivery date for orders placed late in the evening Indian Standard Time (IST). The code incorrectly used the order's UTC timestamp instead of the IST hour to determine whether to add a day to the estimate. The line of code was corrected to use the order's IST hour when checking the dispatch cutoff, fixing the incorrect delivery date calculation.

events.title: Spawning Triage, Locator, Historian subagents in parallel
Historian investigation: delivery estimate cutoff uses UTC hours instead of IST hours

data.rootFinding: Line 34 of src/delivery/estimate.ts checks `orderedAt.getUTCHours() >= DISPATCH_CUTOFF_HOUR` (20). The cutoff is defined in IST time (20:00 IST = 14:30 UTC), but the code compares the raw UTC hour against 20. An order placed at 21:00 IST = 15:30 UTC has UTC hour 15, which is < 20, so the cutoff branch is never taken for any evening-IST order that falls before 20:30 UTC (i.e., before 02:00 IST next day). The `ist` variable IS correctly computed on line 32 via `IST_OFFSET_MS`, but line 34 ignores it and falls back to raw UTC hours.
data.suspiciousPattern: The function correctly shifts the timestamp to IST for the calendar-date extraction (line 32-33) but then reverts to `orderedAt.getUTCHours()` (the unshifted UTC value) for the cutoff comparison on line 34. The fix is: use `ist.getUTCHours()` (the already-shifted Date object) instead of `orderedAt.getUTCHours()`.
data.missingTests: No test in tests/delivery/estimate.test.ts covers an order placed at or after 20:00 IST (14:30 UTC). All existing test times are morning/afternoon IST, so the bug was never caught by the test suite.

data.rootCause: src/delivery/estimate.ts:34 uses orderedAt.getUTCHours() instead of ist.getUTCHours() for the 20:00 IST dispatch cutoff check, making evening orders appear one day early.
data.impact: All orders placed at or after 20:00 IST get a delivery estimate one day too early.

data.subject: perf(delivery): compute IST date without Intl.DateTimeFormat
data.author: GegarinSagolsem

data.expected: For an order placed at 21:00 IST (after the 20:00 IST cutoff), dispatch is the next day (Wed 11 Mar), and delivery is Sat 14 Mar 2026 (3 transit days, skipping Sunday).
data.actual: Cart and order both show Fri 13 Mar 2026 — one day early. The 20:00 IST cutoff is never triggered because the code checks UTC hours (15) instead of IST hours (21).
stepsToReproduce: Set clock to Tuesday 10 March 2026 21:00 IST (15:30 UTC)
Read 'Estimated delivery' line in cart totals — shows Fri 13 Mar instead of Sat 14 Mar
Place order and confirm 'arrives ...' in order history — same wrong date

callers: src/orders/service.ts::placeOrder() — calls estimateDelivery(placedAt), stores wrong date on every evening order
ui/src/cartView.ts — calls estimateDelivery(new Date()) to display estimate in cart
data.notes: Root cause is line 34 of src/delivery/estimate.ts: `orderedAt.getUTCHours()` used instead of `ist.getUTCHours()`. The ist variable is already correctly shifted to IST on line 32 but not used in the cutoff comparison. Test suite has no evening-order (>=20:00 IST) test cases.
